name: Example: Finding Two Linearly Independent Eigenvectors of a 2x2 Matrix
problem:
Given that $\lambda=1$ and $\lambda=-4$ are the eigenvalues of the matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069178/assets/10510533350f1e77e4918cb4aff9edafe5ced005efc845becc8c1558bdd62811.png)
find two linearly independent eigenvectors of $A.$
worked_solution:
We can get two linearly independent eigenvectors by simply finding eigenvectors corresponding to the different eigenvalues.

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A - \lambda I) \textbf{x}=\mathbf{0}.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately. 

- For $\lambda =1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}]-1[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 0 & -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We have to solve the corresponding system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{2}=0 \\ -5{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $2$nd one). So, $x_1$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain  $x_2=0.$ Therefore, the general solution is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069178/assets/97e9cc73b2d39b924618c1372bf680ebf7d4374d1cf4fa9c3bc7e9afc05b06ea.png)
Setting, for instance, $x_1=1,$ we get the eigenvector 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069178/assets/a01037d3f9d9e090010a555fa0e14d6bce72da48c59bd74b0f7dad6afcee71ba.png)

- For $\lambda =-4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}]-(-4)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We have to solve the corresponding system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). So, $x_2$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain $x_1=\dfrac{1}{5}x_2.$ Therefore, the general solution is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069178/assets/34313b24e58011d8be4790d57cd57d4800944903ff16dd20068b45bab2a7d261.png)
Setting, for instance, $x_2=5,$ we get the eigenvector 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069178/assets/cb7300ef2064945937c27944e51032ade506ea16008e22f1a6ab54c5c647812c.png)

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix $A$ are
